findings.title: Login-cache invalidation decision uses the organization-aware (wrapped) model
findings.body: `update()` obtains `idpById` from `getById(...)`, which (when the ORGANIZATION feature is enabled) returns the anonymous `IdentityProviderModel` subclass created by `createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel()`. That wrapper's `isEnabled()` returns `false` whenever the linked organization is disabled or the realm's organization provider is disabled, regardless of the IDP's stored `enabled` flag. `registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate()` then evaluates `LoginFilter.getLoginPredicate()` (which includes `isEnabled`) on this wrapper for `original` and on the raw REST model for `updated`. Consequence: when an org-linked IDP is edited while its organization (or the realm's organization support) is disabled, `test(original)` is false for org reasons and, if the update also makes `test(updated)` false (e.g. setting `broker.public=false` or `hideOnLogin=true`), the login caches are not invalidated at all. The cached ID list, however, was produced by the JPA query which ignores organization enablement, so it still contains that IDP; once the organization is re-enabled, `getForLogin` returns it and consumers only re-check `isEnabled()` (not `hideOnLogin`/`linkOnly`/`broker.public`), so a hidden or non-public broker can be rendered on the login page. The comparison should be done against the raw stored model (e.g. `idpDelegate.getById(model.getInternalId())`).

findings.title: Login cache key omits organizationId, so one entry accumulates one search key per organization
findings.body: `cacheKeyForLogin()` only includes the realm id and the `FetchMode`, and the organization id is used as the *search key* inside a single `IdentityProviderListQuery` entry. For `ORG_ONLY`/`ALL` the organization id varies per login (see `OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean` which calls `getForLogin(ALL, organization.getId())`), so every distinct organization adds a new search key to the same cached object. Each first-time organization hits the `cached == null` branch, which calls `cache.invalidateObject(cacheKey)` (a cluster-wide invalidation that wipes the login cache for that fetch mode on all nodes) and then rebuilds the query copying all previously cached search keys. With N organizations this is O(N^2) copying, one unboundedly growing cache entry per fetch mode, and continuous cluster-wide cache thrashing plus DB re-loads on all nodes. Including the organization id in the cache key (as `getByOrganization` does with `cacheKeyOrgId`) avoids both the growth and the repeated invalidations.

findings.title: Cleanup registered for literal alias "alias" leaks the created identity providers
findings.body: `getCleanup().addCleanup(testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove)` (also at line 425) references the hard-coded alias `"alias"` instead of the alias that was just created (`idp-alias-<i>` / `idp-alias-20`). Consequently (a) none of the 21 identity providers created by `testCacheIDPForLogin` are removed after the test, so they leak into the other test methods that share the same realm and make the exact-count assertions (e.g. `assertEquals(5, ...)` for `REALM_ONLY`) dependent on JUnit method execution order, and (b) the cleanup task itself targets a provider that never existed and will fail with a 404 NotFoundException. Use the actual alias when registering the cleanup.

findings.title: getLoginPredicate() now embeds organization semantics for all its callers
findings.body: `LoginFilter.getLoginPredicate()` is public API in server-spi and is used outside the new invalidation logic (e.g. as the base of `IdentityProviderBean.federatedProviderPredicate()`). Adding `idp.getOrganizationId() == null || Boolean.parseBoolean(idp.getConfig().get(OrganizationModel.BROKER_PUBLIC))` silently changes the result for every existing caller: any IDP that carries an organization id but no `broker.public=true` config is now considered not available for login. Unlike `createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel()` in the Infinispan provider, this check is not guarded by `Profile.Feature.ORGANIZATION`, so in a deployment where the organization feature is disabled but IDPs still carry an organization id (left over from when it was enabled) those brokers disappear from the login/account paths that rely on this predicate. If the organization condition is only needed for cache-invalidation decisions, it should live in the caller or be feature-guarded.

findings.title: No coverage for invalidation on create/remove of a login-eligible IDP, nor for returned results
findings.body: The new test only exercises the negative paths of the invalidation logic added to `create()` and `remove()`: it creates a `hideOnLogin=true` provider and removes a disabled one and asserts the caches survive. The positive paths added in this PR - creating a provider that qualifies for login, and removing one that qualifies - are never exercised, so a regression in `registerIDPLoginInvalidation()` (e.g. stale login lists after adding or deleting a visible broker) would not be caught. The test also only asserts the size of the cached id sets and never compares the stream actually returned by `getForLogin` against the uncached delegate result, so an incorrect set of ids or dropped entries would go unnoticed.
